## Answer: $(0,4\pi]$

I did not fully verify the $H(\alpha)>0$ condition, so the answer rests on the $O(\alpha)$ analysis plus a heuristic for $H$. The endpoint $\alpha=4\pi$ also depends on a Balian–Low-type analogy that I did not prove.

**1. Reduce $O(\alpha)$ to a Gram-matrix problem.** Write $\lambda_{jk}=e^k(1-i\alpha j)$, so $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_{jk}=e^k$. Since $G$ depends only on $\sigma=s+t$, and the measure of $\{s+t\in d\sigma\}$ is $\sigma\,d\sigma$,
$$\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_0^\infty |G|^2\,ds\,dt = 4\int_0^\infty \sigma\Big|\sum_{a} e^{k_a}v_a e^{-\lambda_a\sigma}\Big|^2 d\sigma .$$
Using $\int_0^\infty \sigma e^{-(\lambda+\bar\mu)\sigma}d\sigma=(\lambda+\bar\mu)^{-2}$, the normalized Gram matrix is
$$\frac{4e^{k_a}e^{k_b}}{(\lambda_a+\bar\lambda_b)^2},$$
which is exactly the Gram matrix of the normalized reproducing kernels of the Bergman space $A^2$ of the right half-plane at the points $\lambda_{jk}$. Its diagonal entries are 1, so $O(\alpha)$ is the bottom of the spectrum of this Gram matrix.

**2. Density of the point set.** In the hyperbolic area $dA_h=dA/(\operatorname{Re}z)^2$, the points have uniform density $1/\alpha$: each cell in the $(\log|z|,\arg z)$ coordinates has hyperbolic area exactly $\alpha$. The Bergman kernel is $K(z,z)=1/(4\pi(\operatorname{Re}z)^2)$, so $K(z,z)\,dA=dA_h/(4\pi)$. The critical density (degrees of freedom per unit $K(z,z)\,dA$) is therefore $1/(4\pi)$ per unit $dA_h$.

**3. Consequence for $O(\alpha)$.** When $1/\alpha$ exceeds the critical density, i.e. $\alpha<4\pi$, the normalized kernels are overcomplete and the lower Riesz bound fails, so $O(\alpha)=0$. For $\alpha>4\pi$ the set is sparser than critical and the lower bound holds, so $O(\alpha)>0$. At $\alpha=4\pi$ the density is exactly critical; by analogy with the Fock-space lattice at critical density (Balian–Low type), the lower bound also fails, giving $O(\alpha)=0$. This endpoint is the least certain step.

**4. The condition $H(\alpha)>0$.** I did not establish this rigorously. Heuristically, the $|z+\bar\mu|^2$ term forces the mass of $v$ onto a single vertical line $\operatorname{Re}=|\operatorname{Re}z|$, where the unweighted Hardy Gram is bounded below by a Toeplitz symbol whose infimum is $(4\pi/\alpha)/(e^{4\pi/\alpha}-1)>0$. Cross-line cancellations appear to cost a fixed positive amount in the first term. I therefore take $H(\alpha)>0$ for all $\alpha>0$, which is the assumption the answer depends on.

Combining, $O(\alpha)=0$ exactly when $\alpha\le 4\pi$, and $H(\alpha)>0$ is assumed throughout, giving the set $(0,4\pi]$.

ANSWER: $(0,4\pi]$
